name: Stack granular processors to freeze any short sound into infinite sustain
goal: Turn a short, gappy source into an endless sustained texture: run multi-band or multi-instance granular with linked bands, mild pitch/pan/delay randomization, one voice per band; stack the same granular chain ~4× with independent randomization so gaps fill; follow with upward dynamics (OTT-style), high-pass to stop low buildup, slow random EQ/filter motion, optional diffused 100% wet delay for smear, limiter, and a mono fold-down check.

source.title: Sound Design Trick - Creating Sustained Textures with Granular FX

prerequisites: Any granular FX/processor with density, pitch rand, pan rand, optional multi-band

inputs.name: short_source
inputs.description: Any short synthetic or FOLEY-like hit/texture that does not sustain long enough

outputs.name: infinite_sustain_bed
outputs.description: Forever-running cinematic sustain/texture bed mono-safe enough for point-source use

constraints: Portable granular stacking recipe; plugin names in the source are examples only — recreate with any granular (Portal, Grain, Clouds-class, Web Audio granulator).
Do not redistribute proprietary sample libraries mentioned as demos; the method applies to your own recordings/synths.
Always check mono: these beds often play from a single speaker in trailers.

steps.action: Start from a short source with silence gaps. Insert a granular processor; prefer a dense multi-band or 'schizophrenia-like' starting point, link bands, reduce pitch variation slightly, keep light rand on pitch/pan/delay, ~one voice per band.
steps.expect: Source begins to smear but may still feel like a delay with gaps

steps.action: Stack the same granular treatment about four times in series or parallel. Independent randomization + slowly moving band limits across instances fills holes into a complex continuous sustain.
steps.expect: Texture runs indefinitely after a short build-in

steps.action: Add upward compression/OTT-style processing to lift grain detail, then high-pass — sustained stacks often accumulate unwanted low end.

Animate tone: slow random modulation on a few EQ/filter bands (gentle boosts/cuts, light phasing at low mix, optional talking low-pass on the highs). Keep modulation subtle so it does not read as a phaser solo.
steps.expect: Living timbre without obvious cyclic whoosh

steps.action: Optional smear path: 100% wet diffused delay (modulated delay time) when you want less discrete echoes and more smooth wash. Finish with a limiter to restore level.
steps.expect: Either articulate grains or smeared cloud, both loud enough

steps.action: Sum to mono and confirm the bed still works (point-source playback). Apply the same chain to non-synth sources (pebbles, debris) to verify generality.
steps.expect: Mono fold-down remains usable; method is source-agnostic

verification: After the stack, gaps no longer return to silence for the duration of a long hold.
High-pass prevents booming low buildup under the sustain.
Mono check does not hollow out the bed completely.
